Subject: Sudden 429/5xx surge during our 10k/min ramp test (need urgent help)

Hi Laura —

We executed the staged ramp test we agreed on this morning (10k req/min for 20 minutes, then 30k/min). Around minute 7 of the ramp we started seeing 429s spike to ~12% and a handful of 5xxs. Our client-facing workload experienced timeouts and automated retries kicked off, which amplified the error surface. Attached a screenshot from our monitoring (grafana) and a small sample of the client logs.

Can you confirm whether this is expected behavior under your current rate-limiting policies? We planned this ramp based on the numbers in the MAP and need an ETA for stabilization. This is impacting our demo tomorrow; we need immediate mitigation and a follow-up postmortem.

Thanks —
Alice

Quick triage notes (live):

Observations:
- 429 spike correlated with a burst of concurrent connections from a narrow set of client IPs; retries from the client side amplified throughput and saturated our async request queue for the model shard.
- A small subset of requests saw 5xx (upstream OOM on dedicated GPU pool) — trying to reproduce locally.
- Prefix KV cache hit rate dropped during the ramp, increasing compute per-request.

Immediate mitigations applied (09:31 - 09:35):
1) Enabled short-term per-tenant burst allowance (+30% concurrency) for ACME on the dedicated pool (temporary emergency grant).
2) Rolled a fast fallback routing policy to the compatible smaller model variant (quantized) for ACME route to reduce per-token latency.
3) Rate-limit exception window set for the next 45 minutes while we stabilize; aggressive client-side retry guidance sent to ACME ops.

Next steps:
- Connor: please upload full server-logs-20260818.zip and Grafana snapshots to the ticket.
- I will run the replay and validate that the fallback reduces 429s and keeps 5xxs at 0.
- Investigate whether the kernel selection/quantization path had a pathological performance cliff at certain sequence lengths.

At the moment we should expect degraded error rates to sub-1% after the fallback. If errors persist beyond 30 minutes we escalate to the incident bridge.

-Rishi (SRE)
